subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@cloudfin.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & next steps

Thanks again for taking the time today, Samira  really appreciated the clarity on CloudFin's priorities. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we're all aligned.

Key pain points you mentioned:
- High per-query cost on current embedding + reranking pipeline (especially for chat-like flows).
- Latency spikes during peak business hours impacting SLAs for underwriting agents.
- Fragmented observability (hard to correlate model version changes with regressions).

Goals you outlined:
- Reduce per-inference unit cost by ~30% without sacrificing accuracy for reranking.
- Achieve 95th percentile latency under 200ms for 1kQPS baseline.
- Centralize model rollout telemetry and automated rollback for regressions.

How Redwood maps to that (summary):
- Embeddings + reranking: Recommend moving to our batch-optimized embedding pipeline with prefetch + KV cache for user/session prefixes; will cut token-level cost and reduce cold-starts.
- Streaming + function calling: We can stream structured outputs directly to your UI and use function-calling hooks for deterministic downstream actions (e.g., tagging, routing).
- SDK changes: Minor client update to enable continuous batching and structured-output schemas (we provide adapters for your current SDK).
- Observability: Per-route dashboards + automatic sample tracing we showed today; can attach evals to prompt sets for regression alerts.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) I attached a short milestones doc with a 6-week pilot scope (Redwood-integration-milestones.xlsx). Can you review by EOD Friday?
2) Security/compliance: I'll loop in our security pack (SOC2-summary.pdf) and connect to your procurement team for the data access checklist.
3) Technical deep-dive: Schedule a 60-min session for your infra + ML engineer next week (I proposed Thu 4/29  calendar invite link below).

If that looks right, we'll prep the pilot environment (dedicated test pool), a simple SDK PR for your frontend, and a sample eval set to measure reranking precision before/after.

Thanks  excited to keep this moving.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Attachments: Redwood-integration-milestones.xlsx, SOC2-summary.pdf

From: Samira Khan <samira.k@cloudfin.com>

Cc: CloudFin - Procurement <procurement@cloudfin.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & next steps

Thanks Marissa  this is a great summary and matches what we discussed. A few quick replies: 

- Milestones doc: I'll review with the ML team and get back by Friday EOD.
- Security: Procurement will want the SOC2 summary and a data flow diagram. Procurement is CC'd  can you share an S3 link or Drive?
- Deep-dive: Thu 4/29 at 10:30 PT works for us; please send calendar invite.

On the technical asks: our ML lead is specifically concerned about how you handle KV cache consistency across pod restarts and whether the streaming path supports partial JSON outputs that our UI can hydrate incrementally. Could Rishi cover that in the deep-dive?

Thanks  Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Product, Search + Personalization
CloudFin
samira.k@cloudfin.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.k@cloudfin.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 17:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & next steps

Got it  I'll take the technical deep-dive. Quick notes to prep: 
- KV cache consistency: we use a write-through metadata log and per-session sequence checkpoints; on pod restart the runtime replays the last-known sequence and validates KV headers. For the pilot we'll instrument extra health checks and expose a checkpoint metric.
- Streaming partial JSON: our structured-output streaming sends well-formed chunked JSON where each chunk is a complete (small) JSON object you can append to the UI. We also include an end-of-stream marker to validate completeness.

I'll prepare a short slide (2-3 diagrams) and a lightweight demo. Marissa  I'll need the CloudFin test keys and a point-of-contact for infra (Samira, who should I ask for that?).

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
